solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I degenerate when getting raised awareness all of a sudden

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the pieces lifts them so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to degenerate is to rot or decay
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to declining while being told their consciousness has been suddenly heightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting raised' turns IROTAS upwards. SATORI is the Zen Buddhist term for sudden enlightenment.
explanation.definitionFit: In Zen Buddhism the word names a flash of sudden enlightenment, an abrupt awakening of understanding.

clue.text: Say something abstract out loud when Phil goes and gets set

indicators.note: Phil goes means the letters of the name Phil leave the front of the word
spoken out loud, so the remaining letters are judged by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: to philosophise is to say something abstract; its form 'philosophises', said quickly, is heard as 'philosophies'
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: When Phil leaves the conversation, the abstract talk hardens into fixed views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out loud' respells the spoken word as PHILOSSIFIES; 'goes' then drops PHIL from its front. 'Say' looks like an example marker but belongs to the phrase meaning philosophise.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is to turn to bone, or figuratively to harden and become fixed, so something that does so sets.

clue.text: Unstable time and very hard stuff an unhappy American brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing the whole string up means it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard, and HH is very hard
to stuff is to cram
unhappy means sad

explanation.surface: A mixed-up American lugs up a period of rough hard material, sounding like an unsteady tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses ERAHHCRAMASADAM. HH is the pencil grading for very hard lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone utterly crazy, after the wild behaviour of hares in the breeding season; unstable fits that madness.

clue.text: Untidy heap around grave and nearby inscription

indicators.note: the jumbled heap is placed around the other piece, enclosing it
an untidy heap has its letters in disorder, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a grave is a pit dug in the earth

explanation.surface: A messy mound of earth surrounds a burial plot, with some lettering close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' gives E...APH, split around the hole. 'nearby' refers back to the grave already in the clue: the inscription stands at it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the commemorative text carved on a tombstone, which stands at the burial place.

clue.text: Disloyal quality enables senators to be corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted letters have been tampered with, so these two words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Something lets lawmakers be bribed, an unpatriotic trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the condition of being treacherous towards one's country, so it is a quality of betrayal.

clue.text: Ranting actor allowed Danish role

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overplays and rants
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A bombastic performer was permitted to play the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic prince of Denmark is the title part of his best-known play.

clue.text: Scotsman's fixation with odd losses

indicators.note: losing the odd letters keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the word fixation

explanation.surface: A man from Scotland has an obsession that comes with strange setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scottish form of the name John, so its bearer is typically a Scot.

clue.text: Grub Street area's odd characters recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the pieces are read backwards
the odd characters of the word area are its first and third letters

explanation.surface: Grub Street, London's old haunt of hack writers, has its peculiar residents remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub Street' looks like one place name, but 'Grub' alone is the definition. 'recalled' reverses STAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is slang for food, and so is the plural noun here, as in 'let's get some ___'.

clue.text: A rather quiet sound is increased by this

parts.note: mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately quiet

explanation.surface: A soft noise gets louder thanks to some device.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for amplifier, the device boosts the volume of an audio signal.

clue.text: No one in fury repeatedly exposes president

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and 'no one in' means every I is removed from the words for fury and repeatedly

parts.note: ire is fury
again means once more, repeatedly

explanation.surface: Nobody, in a recurring rage, unmasks a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: IRE AGAIN loses both its Is (one is I in Roman numerals), leaving the answer; 'exposes' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States, serving through the 1980s.

clue.text: In W Indian region, twerp who rode bareback?

indicators.note: the twerp is placed in the region, inside its letters

parts.note: Goa is a state on the west coast of India
a div is British slang for a stupid person, a twerp

explanation.surface: An idiot from western India rides a horse without a saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'W Indian' suggests the West Indies, but it means western India. 'bareback' is a pun: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the noblewoman rode through Coventry unclothed, so her back was literally bare as she rode.

clue.text: In Lille, he boards Eurostar, say, and initially goes at the back

indicators.note: boards means gets on, so this piece goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: Eurostar is an example of a train, the one under the Channel
il is French for he, as spoken in Lille

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of the word goes

explanation.surface: A man boards the cross-Channel express in Lille and starts by heading for the rear carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Lille, he' asks for French: il. Eurostar is the passenger train service through the Channel Tunnel between London and the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing means lagging behind, following in the rear position of a group.

clue.text: Perhaps people conspiring to hack graphic devices

definitions.meaning: whimsically, schemers who plot digitally, as when breaking into computers
machines that draw graphs or drawings under computer control

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means pen-driven drawing machines run from a computer; whimsically it means schemers working by computer.

clue.text: What's commonest in barrels aged the whiskey

parts.note: R appears twice in the word barrels, more often than any other letter
ye is the old-fashioned form of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'

explanation.surface: What is most typical in casks that have matured the spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonest in barrels' sounds like a statistic about casks, but it is the letter occurring most in that word.
explanation.definitionFit: This grain is the base of a style of American and Canadian whiskey, which takes its name.

clue.text: Heavenly saints, each half-lost, out of Paradise

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
half-lost means the word Heavenly keeps only its back half, its front half lost
each extends the same half-loss to the word saints, which keeps its front half

explanation.surface: Holy saints, each half-forgotten, are banished from Heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' looks like the definition, but it is fodder: ENLY and SAI, the surviving halves, are put 'out' of order.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to Elysium, the Greek afterlife paradise for heroes, so it means belonging to paradise.

clue.text: Privy Council veto NGO's conclusions

indicators.note: the conclusions of the words are their final letters

explanation.surface: The monarch's advisory body blocks a charity's findings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privy Council' reads as one body, the British monarch's advisers, but 'Privy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A privy is an outdoor lavatory, and the British slang word for a lavatory fits it.

clue.text: Skimmed folio about stopping destiny

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: destiny is fate
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A leaf of a book, skimmed through, concerns blocking one's fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimmed' reads as a verb about reading the folio quickly, but it is the definition, as in skimmed milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimmed milk has had its cream removed, leaving it free of fat.

clue.text: It's not very important to pay bill (as Americans would have it)

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay
what Americans call a bill, a piece of paper money, the British call a note

explanation.surface: Settling the account matters little, American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay bill' suggests foot the bill, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A note at the bottom of a page carries a minor detail, so the word also means something of little significance.

clue.text: Politician immediately about to have a parliamentary place set up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: stat, from Latin statim, means immediately in medical jargon

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means reading the letters upwards

parts.note: to sit is to have a seat in parliament

explanation.surface: A politician has to take a seat in the House at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Stat is medical shorthand for at once, from Latin statim; an MP is said to sit for a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A statist is a supporter of state control, and an old word for a statesman or political figure.

clue.text: Plain situation requiring a microscope?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, when the thing to be viewed is tiny, there is little there to see

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone unattractive; literally it describes something so small that it needs magnifying.

clue.text: Brother turns in man that won't yield, possibly an ally

definitions.meaning: describing something hard and unbending, as stone is
an ally is a type of playing marble, so it is an example

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: turns means the abbreviation is turned round, read backwards

explanation.surface: A sibling switches sides inside a stubborn man who may be a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ally' looks like a friend, but in the game of marbles an ally is a choice marble, originally made of alabaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone is hard and unyielding, and a playing ally is one sort of small glass or stone ball.

clue.text: First Labour's place secures vote over ruthless cost-cutters

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, so the letters read upwards
secures means holds inside, so the vote goes into the place

parts.note: Hercules' first labour was killing the lion of Nemea
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: The leading party's office secures a ballot result against brutal budget slashers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Labour' looks like the political party, but it is Hercules' first task. X goes inside NEMEA after the first E, and 'over' reverses NEMEXA.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, those who wield the axe make sweeping cuts to budgets and jobs.

clue.text: Lid that collapses partly caught a hare poacher from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the letters are read starting at the back
partly means only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A poacher was caught, partly, with a hare, seen from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes TAHAREPO from the words, and 'from behind' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsible top hat, a gibus, is folded flat to store under a theatre seat; lid is slang for hat.

clue.text: Top of phone exposed to prepare for selfie?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top of the word phone is its first letter

parts.note: out means exposed, revealed

explanation.surface: A phone's upper part is left uncovered when getting ready for a self-portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the lips forward is a stock pose struck for a self-portrait photo, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Site of historic drownings needs new stakes

parts.note: antes are poker stakes put in before the deal

explanation.surface: A place of past drownings needs fresh posts driven in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stakes' suggests wooden posts, but here they are gambling stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: During the Terror of 1793 to 1794, prisoners in this French city were drowned en masse in the Loire.

clue.text: Online address retained by the female member of Irish sports team

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so this piece sits within the other

parts.note: her refers to the female
a URL is a web address

explanation.surface: A woman keeps a web link to her Irish sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurling is an Irish field game played with sticks, and a hurler plays it.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of hurling, the Gaelic stick-and-ball game, belongs to an Irish sports team.

clue.text: Find out location of LA

definitions.meaning: LA, Louisiana, is in the ..., the southern United States

explanation.definitionFit: The verb is slang for discovering or working out; split as S US it gives the southern United States.

clue.text: Kojak? Which part of that best matches his head?

definitions.meaning: the TV detective Kojak's first name, given as an example

definitions.text: Which part of that best matches his head?
definitions.meaning: split as '...', the letter O in Kojak, round like his bald head

explanation.definitionFit: Telly Savalas played Lieutenant Theo Kojak; split 3,1, the name points to the round letter in Kojak, like his bald pate.
